# Results — Study 180 (TRIX) on real daily tape

and signal-line cross (TRIX vs its 9-day EMA), tested on five liquid ETFs/equities
(SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, MSFT), daily bars, with fixed-horizon forward returns and a
random-direction control on the same entry bars.  As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## The honest test — zero-line cross, 20-day hold, gross (cost = 0)

A direction-fair payoff: the only structure the TRIX zero-line cross can harvest is whether
the newly confirmed trend direction predicts the next 20 trading days.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TRIX zero-line cross** | 428 | **48.4%** | **+8.00** | — | **+0.34** |
| Random direction (control) | 428 | 47.9% | −43.01 | — | −1.60 |

- The TRIX zero-line cross earns **+8.00 bps/trade** gross, HAC *t* = **+0.34** — statistically
  indistinguishable from zero.  No inference bar is cleared.
- The cross-minus-random delta is **+51.02 bps**, but this reflects the control being negative
  (the control had an unlucky seed during a predominantly upward market period where the same
  entry timing with random direction underperformed) — not a genuine directional signal from TRIX.
- Per-instrument: every |*t*| ≤ 1.41 (SPY +0.32, QQQ +0.07, IWM +0.13, AAPL +1.03, MSFT −1.41).
  The cross carries no systematic directional information.

## Signal-line cross (TRIX vs 9-day EMA of TRIX), 10-day hold

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TRIX signal-line cross** | 942 | **50.6%** | **−18.58** | **−1.55** |
| Random direction (control) | 942 | 53.1% | +34.38 | +2.85 |

The signal-line cross is directionally *negative* (t = −1.55) while the same-entry random
control is positive — a sign that the TRIX signal-line cross systematically points the *wrong*
way at these entries, likely because the shorter signal-line horizon (10d) captures reversals
after the heavy-lag TRIX "confirms" an already-exhausted trend.

## Hold-period sweep (zero-line cross, gross)

| Hold | n | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d  | 428 | +8.04 | +0.59 | 51.9% |
| 10d | 428 | +15.16 | +0.79 | 51.9% |
| 20d | 428 | +8.00 | +0.34 | 48.4% |
| 40d | 428 | −5.89 | −0.21 | 48.4% |
| 60d | 428 | −6.28 | −0.19 | 50.0% |

No holding window produces a HAC |*t*| ≥ 2.  The best is 0.79 at 10 days — well below
the inference bar.  The signal is invariably noise, regardless of how long you hold.

## Period sensitivity (zero-line cross, hold=20d, gross)

| TRIX period | n | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 9  | 707 | +21.41 | +1.27 |
| 15 | 428 | +8.00  | +0.34 |
| 21 | 296 | +20.06 | +0.68 |
| 30 | 177 | −19.90 | −0.44 |

The highest *t* across four period variations is 1.27 (period=9).  Under a Bonferroni
correction for four hypotheses, the threshold is |*t*| ≥ 2.57 — not approached anywhere.
This is consistent with data dredging noise, not a real signal.

## Cost sweep (zero-line cross, hold=20d)

| Round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +8.00 | +0.34 |
| 1.0 bps | +7.00 | +0.30 |
| 2.0 bps | +6.00 | +0.25 |
| 5.0 bps | +3.00 | +0.13 |

The t-stat is already below 1 at zero cost, so costs simply make an already insignificant
strategy more negative.  At ~6 zero-line crosses per instrument per year, turnover is low
(≈30 trades/yr across the basket) — the signal dies not from costs but from the absence
of any directional information.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.**  Zero-line cross: gross +8 bps/trade, HAC *t* = +0.34.  Signal-line
  cross: gross −19 bps/trade, *t* = −1.55.  No holding window, period, or signal variant
  clears |*t*| ≥ 2.  Per-instrument, every |*t*| ≤ 1.41.  Bonferroni-corrected threshold
  (four period variants) not approached.  The triple smoothing creates lag that confirms
  moves *after* they have already happened.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.**  The gross expectancy is statistically indistinguishable from zero
  across all parameter settings, so no positive net edge exists.  At low turnover (~6 zero-line
  crosses/yr per instrument), costs are not the killer — the signal simply does not exist.
- **Triple-smoothing: `CONFIRMED LAG, NO EDGE`.**  The heavy lag from three sequential EMAs
  does not filter false signals more effectively than a random direction; it just delays the
  entry until much of the trend has already been priced in.
